page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-6 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine within the GPU Machines family. The instance is powered by an x86_64 processor architecture featuring 6 dedicated vCPUs paired with 22.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.67 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is not bundled locally, indicating that persistent disk volumes or network-attached storage solutions must be configured separately to host the operating system and application data.

The defining element of the g4-standard-6 hardware profile is its fractional GPU partition, delivering one-eighth (0.125) of an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell-generation accelerator. This fractional allocation is configured with 12 GB of dedicated GPU VRAM. By slicing the underlying enterprise GPU, the instance offers access to modern workstation and graphics acceleration capabilities without requiring the provisioning or cost overhead of a full dedicated graphics card.

Because the server includes fractional GPU resources and lacks integrated local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, it represents a targeted entry-level graphics platform. It is engineered primarily for graphics-focused applications, remote visual workstations, lightweight machine learning inference, and 3D rendering workloads where full physical GPU allocation would result in underutilized hardware.
description: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-6 is a graphics-optimized compute instance designed for entry-level GPU tasks within the GPU Machines family. Running on an x86_64 architecture, it provides 6 dedicated vCPUs and 22.0 GB of memory, yielding 3.67 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is equipped with a fractional 0.125 share of an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell accelerator coupled with 12 GB of dedicated GPU VRAM. It includes no bundled local storage, necessitating external network storage for runtime environments and persistent data, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By provisioning a slice of an enterprise-grade GPU rather than a dedicated physical card, the g4-standard-6 provides a cost-efficient resource footprint suited for remote graphics workstations, lightweight 3D rendering, and entry-level model inference tasks.
